news.summary_en: Intuit has reached an agreement to sell its email-marketing subsidiary Mailchimp to Italian technology consolidator Bending Spoons for $3.68 billion in cash and stock, slated for closure in early 2027. This divestiture, representing a loss of over 70% from the $12 billion acquisition price in 2021, follows Mailchimp's stagnant revenue growth and its role as a drag on Intuit's broader financial valuation.
paragraphs: Tax software maker Intuit said Thursday that it has agreed to sell marketing subsidiary Mailchimp to Italian technology consolidator Bending Spoons for $3.68 billion in cash and stock. The deal is set to close in early 2027, according to a statement.

The sale is a costly retreat for Intuit, which paid $12 billion for Mailchimp in 2021 in a push beyond its core tax and accounting businesses. Five years later, the software maker is unloading the email-marketing company for less than one-third of that price after Mailchimp became a drag on its overall revenue growth.

The deal is the latest instance of Bending Spoons picking up a once promising technology asset. The company bought productivity software startup Airtable in September for 10% of what it was once worth.
The Bending Spoons portfolio also contains AOL, Brightcove, Eventbrite, Evernote, Meetup, Vimeo, and WeTransfer.

In August Intuit started running Mailchimp as a distinct operating segment. The move was meant to give investors more transparency as the company tried to manage the unit for profitability, Sandeep Aujla, Intuit's finance chief, said at a September company briefing.

Also on Thursday, Intuit announced stronger-than-expected earnings and revenue for its fiscal first quarter, which ended on Oct. 31. The company reported $2.91 in adjusted earnings per share on $4.35 billion in revenue. Analysts polled by LSEG were looking for $2.70 per share and $4.31 billion in revenue.
While Intuit's revenue increased 12% year over year, Mailchimp revenue declined 1% to $313 million. Analysts polled by StreetAccount had expected $314.4 million.

Management called for $22.88 to $23.12 in adjusted earnings per share for the 2027 fiscal year, with $23.081 billion to $23.365 billion in revenue. Analysts polled by LSEG had predicted $23.62 in adjusted earnings per share on $23.43 billion in revenue. Intuit shares tumbled 15% in extended trading.

The company said Mailchimp should produce $1.256 billion to $1.266 billion in fiscal 2027 revenue, which would be down 1% to flat year over year. In August Aujla said Intuit anticipated Mailchimp's higher effective prices offsetting increased client churn. Mailchimp was founded in 2001. Rivals include Klaviyo, which went public in 2023.
Berkshire Hathaway invested $600 million in Bending Spoons when the acquirer went public in July, and in October Bending Spoons said Berkshire invested another $330 million.

news.author: Cybersecurity Dive
news.content_snippet:
Michael LoSapio, a Palantir executive, also denied that the U.S. Capitol was attacked on Jan. 6, 2021.

President Donald Trump’s nominee to lead the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency offered little information about how he would steer the beleaguered agency during his confirmation hearing on Thursday.

Michael LoSapio, the chief information security officer at the data analytics firm Palantir, provided only high-level answers to members of the Senate Homeland Security Committee wh
news.summary_en: Michael LoSapio, CISO of Palantir and Trump’s nominee for CISA director, faced significant scrutiny during his Senate Homeland Security Committee confirmation hearing. He evaded questions regarding the administration’s budget cuts to CISA and denied the nature of the January 6, 2021 Capitol attack, raising alarms among lawmakers about his political alignment and commitment to agency autonomy.

news.author: Amy Chang Chien
news.content_snippet:
Few things could generate more buzz for a small restaurant than a visit from Jensen Huang. In recent years, the former Nvidia CEO became known for dining out at street markets and hole-in-the-wall noodle joints across Asia, drawing huge crowds of fans and photographers wherever he went.

But after Huang resigned last week amid revelations of multiple extramarital affairs, some of the food vendors he helped put on the map are wondering whether their most famous customer is still good for business
news.summary_en: Jensen Huang has resigned as CEO of Nvidia following allegations of multiple extramarital affairs. The incident has triggered widespread public scrutiny, with small businesses in Taipei weighing the reputational impact of their past association with him against the marketing value of his high-profile visits.
paragraphs: Few things could generate more buzz for a small restaurant than a visit from Jensen Huang. In recent years, the former Nvidia CEO became known for dining out at street markets and hole-in-the-wall noodle joints across Asia, drawing huge crowds of fans and photographers wherever he went.

But after Huang resigned last week amid revelations of multiple extramarital affairs, some of the food vendors he helped put on the map are wondering whether their most famous customer is still good for business. In Taiwan, where Huang was born and his dining habits have long been a spectator sport, many say they aren't ready to turn against their hometown hero.

Tu Chang-chun, the owner of Ice World, a shaved-ice shop in Taipei, describes Huang as friendly, the kind of person who puts others around him at ease. His impression of the billionaire hasn’t changed since he learned of his affair with Alice Huang, a businesswoman accused of spying for China.

“It’s not as if he killed someone or set something on fire. Why blow it all out of proportion?” Tu said on Monday evening, standing beneath the yellow lights of his stall at Linjiang Street Night Market. “Now, a lot of foreigners walk past, see my sign, and laugh. People just love kicking someone when they’re down.”

At the entrance of his shop, Tu continues to proudly display a photo of Huang posing with him and his wife. “I think he’s such a warm and approachable person,” Tu added. “Why are people treating him this way?”
Jensen Huang has visited this shaved ice stall at Taipei’s Linjiang Street Night Market three times since 2023.

Tu says that Huang has visited his shop three times since 2023, and he always orders the same thing: mango shaved ice with tangyuan (sticky rice balls). The dessert, a blend of tropical fruit and condensed milk, is popular in Taipei’s bustling night markets, especially among first-time visitors to the island.
“When he came in for shaved ice, he would spend half an hour eating a single bowl,” recalled Tu. “Whenever someone came up to take a photo with him, he got right up. He’s not pretentious.”

At a tofu pudding shop near Ningxia Night Market in western Taipei, photos of Huang remain on display alongside those of other prominent technology figures who have visited, including Morris Chang, the founder of Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC). The store manager, Hsieh, defended the shop’s decision to keep them up.
“I don’t think this changes the fact that he’s a very successful businessman,” Hsieh said of Huang’s affairs with Alice Huang and other women. “Having an affair is a private matter.”

Hsieh, who agreed to be identified only by his surname for privacy reasons, said that Huang had visited the shop four times over the past few years, and on each occasion he seemed friendly and down-to-earth.
Owner Tu Chang-chun said he has no plans to take down photos Jensen Huang visiting his shaved-ice shop.

In Taiwan, Huang’s culinary indulgences extended well beyond street food. He frequented some of Taipei’s most exclusive restaurants, where he hosted technology executives for what became known in the local press as “Trillion-Dollar Banquets,” a reference to the attendees’ combined net worth of more than 1 trillion New Taiwan dollars.

The dinners often drew crowds of journalists and photographers hoping to catch a glimpse of Huang and his guests. The intense media attention helps explain why so many photographs and videos of Huang with Alice Huang were captured in Taiwan. Restaurant owners, meanwhile, welcomed the publicity, often proudly displaying photographs of themselves with Huang inside their establishments.

The Taiwanese tea chain 19 Tea House launched a new drink this week, giving it a name that pokes fun at Huang’s alleged “womanizing” ways. According to the chain, the drink combines osmanthus-infused honey with fresh lemon, offering a blend of fragrant floral notes and sweet-and-tangy citrus flavors.

Support for Huang in Taiwan has also extended far beyond the restaurants he frequented. On Monday evening, Taipei 101, the island’s iconic skyscraper just blocks from one of Huang’s favorite night markets, lit up with messages of support for the former Nvidia CEO, including “Taiwan ♡ Jensen,” “Family ♡ Friendship,” “Thrive Together,” and “Taiwan AI Build Future Together.”

Tech industry figures who supported the initiative told Taiwan’s state-run Central News Agency that the illumination campaign was intended to “help restore Jensen Huang’s reputation,” urging the public not to “kick him when he's down, but instead offer warmth and support during the autumn and winter.”
This is an edition of the Model Behavior newsletter. Read previous newsletters here.

news.title: Man hired by Russia spied on Silicon Valley tech and defense company, feds say
news.title_en: Man hired by Russia spied on Silicon Valley tech and defense company, feds say
news.author: Dan Goodin
news.content_snippet:

news.summary_en: Igor D’iu, a 25-year-old Russian national, has been indicted for espionage after illegally entering the U.S. to surveil employees of a Silicon Valley defense tech firm, widely identified as Palantir. The defendant allegedly gathered intelligence on the company's military support and weapon supply chain to Ukraine.
paragraphs: A Russian national has been indicted on suspicions he was a Russian spy who stalked and surveilled employees of a Silicon Valley company that was assisting Ukraine in its ongoing war with its western neighbor.

Igor D’iu, 25, allegedly photographed the employees and their computer screens as they worked at a coffee shop located near the company’s Palo Alto office, federal prosecutors said Wednesday. He also kept a list of home addresses of employees and a senior executive. At one point, prosecutors said, D’iu trailed an employee as she traveled home from Palo Alto to San Francisco. An affidavit filed in the case referred to the employee as FEMP1, short for female employee, and said the event left her “in a state of emotional distress.”
### Evasive and irregular turns

“FEMP1 made evasive and irregular turns, took back roads, and turned into a grocery store parking lot where D’IU continued aggressively following her vehicle,” an FBI special agent wrote. “D’IU followed FEMP1 through U-turns, illegal left turns, and ran a red light to stay with FEMP1 for nearly thirty miles. FEMP1 called 911 while driving and was instructed to drive directly to San Francisco Police Department (“SFPD”) Mission Station. Near SFPD Mission Station, FEMP1 flagged an SFPD patrol vehicle and reported the incident. D’IU left once FEMP1 made contact with the patrol vehicle.”

When police later questioned D’iu about the incident, the defendant allegedly said he saw a woman get into a car and thought she was “beautiful.” He then told the investigators that he followed her because he “wanted to ask her out on a date.”

Prosecutors didn’t name the company, but both Reuters and Bloomberg, citing unnamed people with knowledge of the case, identified it as Palantir. Ars is unable to confirm that reporting. Palantir representatives didn’t respond to an email seeking confirmation.

D’iu allegedly entered the US unlawfully in the summer of 2026 after being recruited by someone over Telegram. Prosecutors said the party gave D’iu a clandestine assignment to target employees of a large technology and defense company. D’iu received instructions, equipment, and financial support along with information that his work was on behalf of “the motherland.” His instructions were to collect information about the company because it was supplying weapons for use against Russian forces in Ukraine.

Prosecutors said D’iu traveled from Istanbul, Turkey, to Mexico City in June. He then crossed the border into the US and was instructed to buy laptops, cell phones, wireless networking equipment, and remote access software. Besides instructions to monitor company employees at the coffee shop, D’iu’s orders also included positioning his laptop at certain locations near the company so it could be remotely accessed in an attempt to collect information from company employees nearby.

D’iu allegedly obtained fraudulent identification documents to conceal his identity as he conducted his activities. The documents included a falsified California ID card, an altered US passport, and a Social Security card bearing the assumed name of “Hugo Landry Johns.” The passport was allegedly an authentic US passport that originally had been issued to someone elsewhere in the country. It was modified to display D’iu’s photograph and assumed identity.

D’iu was arrested on October 30 and remains in custody. He is charged with one count of Conspiracy to Act as an Agent of a Foreign Government, one count of Acting as an Agent of a Foreign Government Without Notice to the Attorney General, and one count of Interstate Stalking. If convicted for Acting as an Agent of a Foreign Government Without Notice to the Attorney General, he faces a maximum sentence of 10 years in prison, a fine of $250,000, and three years of supervised release. He faces a maximum sentence of five years in prison, a fine of $250,000, and three years of supervised release for each conviction on the other two charges.
D’iu had his initial appearance in federal court on November 2. He is next scheduled to appear in federal court on November 24.

news.title: Meta’s Muse Charm might cost $300
news.title_en: Meta’s Muse Charm might cost $300
news.author: Jay Peters
news.content_snippet:
Meta is planning to price the Muse Charm, a little gadget with a screen that lets you chat with your Muse AI agent, at $300, according to The Information. CEO Mark Zuckerberg revealed the gadget earlier this year and said the company expected to ship the Charm “in time for the holidays in December,” but he didn’t provide a price at the time.

When he announced the Muse Charm, Zuckerberg said that the company had “packed the whole Muse experience,” including real-time voice and avatar technology,
news.summary_en: Meta plans to launch the Muse Charm, a wearable device featuring real-time voice and avatar interaction, at a $300 price point by this December. The device integrates a fingerprint sensor for instant AI agent access without smartphone intervention and includes a 12-month complimentary 5G data plan from Verizon, while Meta has deferred its internal smartwatch project until 2027.
paragraphs: Meta is planning to price the Muse Charm, a little gadget with a screen that lets you chat with your Muse AI agent, at $300, according to The Information. CEO Mark Zuckerberg revealed the gadget earlier this year and said the company expected to ship the Charm “in time for the holidays in December,” but he didn’t provide a price at the time.

When he announced the Muse Charm, Zuckerberg said that the company had “packed the whole Muse experience,” including real-time voice and avatar technology, into the gadget. It has a fingerprint sensor, and you can tap it to be able to talk to a Muse AI agent without unlocking a phone or opening an app. The Information reports that the Muse Charm will come with a free 12-month 5G data plan from Verizon.

Spokesperson Tyler Yee wrote to The Information that “We’re charmed by the interest in our AI devices, and we’ll have more to share soon.” When reached for comment by The Verge, Yee provided the same statement.
The company is also working on a smartwatch, The Information says, but a launch for that has been pushed to 2027 as Meta tries to get Muse Charm out the door.
Meta also open sourced code to let users make their own Muse gadgets, which my colleague Sean Hollister used to make his own DIY Muse Charm.
Update, November 19th: Noted statement given by Meta spokesperson Tyler Yee.

Based on the GIF shared by Stein, it looks like you can open the sidebar by clicking the gray bar that appears on the left side of your screen. From there, Google will show a list of the searches you’ve made using AI Mode, along with the ability to start a new thread, search your threads, or
paragraphs: Google is updating its homepage to include AI searches. In a post on X, Google’s vice president of product, Robby Stein, shows how you can now open a collapsible sidebar to view and continue your AI chats.

Based on the GIF shared by Stein, it looks like you can open the sidebar by clicking the gray bar that appears on the left side of your screen. From there, Google will show a list of the searches you’ve made using AI Mode, along with the ability to start a new thread, search your threads, or connect a Gemini Notebook.

It’s yet another big change for Google’s homepage, which has long presented you with a single bar to kick off your web search. The company brought its AI Mode button to its search bar last year, which opens up a chatbot-like search experience within Google. In May, Google updated its search box to accommodate longer queries and added AI-powered autocomplete.

Stein says Google is rolling out the option because “people are coming to Search with more questions that aren’t just one and done,” adding that “in testing, this sidebar made a big difference for making progress & continuing to explore the web.” The new homepage is rolling out globally on desktop.

news.summary_en: Ramp AI Index and OpenRouter data indicate that US corporate AI usage is hitting record highs while the average cost per million tokens has dropped below $0.45 due to aggressive pricing competition. Anthropic has surpassed OpenAI in both spending and volume market share, signaling a paradigm shift in the AI infrastructure market from a high-premium phase to a defensive pricing cycle.
paragraphs: US companies are using AI models more intensively than ever and paying less for the privilege.

The latest update of the Ramp AI Index, which draws on transaction data from more than 85,000 US companies, lays out the numbers. Tokens, the units of computation in which AI providers bill model usage, got 21.2 percent cheaper in six weeks, according to Ramp lead economist Ara Kharazian. At the same time, token volume rose 1.5 percent to a record high.

Token spending, meaning what companies actually pay for AI APIs, fell 6.3 percent from its peak two weeks earlier. Month over month (the week ending November 15 vs. the week ending October 18), total token spending still rose 12 percent, but token volume jumped 27.2 percent over the same span. The gap between usage and revenue keeps widening.

The average price per million tokens for OpenAI and Anthropic combined fell to $0.45, according to Ramp, down 11.2 percent from the prior month. OpenAI is cheaper at $0.38 per million tokens compared with $0.50 for Anthropic.

API routing platform OpenRouter shows a similar pattern. According to an analysis Peter Walker published on X, weekly token volume for closed-weight models from OpenAI, Anthropic and Google grew 1,215 percent since the start of 2026. Weekly spending rose 455 percent over the same period, far more slowly. The spending peak came in the week of October 5, according to the OpenRouter data, which runs through the week of November 9. Spending has been declining since then.

Ramp's token metrics rely on usage and billing data imported from AI providers, while OpenRouter measures traffic through its API routing platform. The fact that both sources show a spending peak in October followed by declining outlays and rising volume reinforces the trend, though neither service is representative of the overall market. OpenRouter in particular offers only a narrow window into a very specific user base.
### Anthropic dominates the token market on IPO day

In the week ending November 15, 2026, Anthropic accounted for 58.7 percent of all token spending, according to the Ramp AI Index, up 1.7 percentage points from the prior month. Its share of token volume was even higher at 59.4 percent. OpenAI fell to 37.2 percent of spending and 37.7 percent of volume. Google came in at 1.4 percent and xAI (SpaceXAI) at 2.4 percent.
Kharazian wrote on X that Anthropic holds this share on IPO day. In October, however, Anthropic's token spending grew only 0.5 percent month over month, while OpenAI's grew 2.1 percent.

In October 2026, 56.8 percent of all tracked US companies paid for AI products or services, according to Ramp, up one percentage point from September and 13.3 percentage points more than a year earlier. Anthropic leads with an adoption rate of 44.8 percent, while OpenAI sits at 40.6 percent.
### Stripe data also shows strong AI growth and signs of cooling

The Ramp AI Index tracks the demand side, what companies spend on AI. Payment processor Stripe has published its own AI Index that measures the supply side: incoming payments at roughly 20,000 AI companies that use Stripe.

According to the Stripe AI Index, revenue at AI companies grew 103 percent over the 52 weeks ending November 8. The typical (median) AI company grew only 41 percent, though, suggesting that a few large providers are skewing the overall picture.

The slowdown over shorter time frames is pronounced. Annualized over 13 weeks, growth stood at about 80 percent, down from 140 percent just a few months ago. The US leads with 104 percent year-over-year growth, while the EU sits at 67 percent. AI companies are growing far faster than traditional software firms, according to Stripe: 103 percent compared with 33 percent in the SaaS Index.

Both indexes paint a similar picture. AI is still growing fast, but momentum is cooling. At Ramp, that shows up through falling prices and concentrated demand. At Stripe, it shows up through slowing growth rates on the provider side.

New growth could emerge from more capable or more reliable models, or simply from better integration of current models into business workflows. The potential is there, considering how AI has upended the entire coding market in a matter of months. The AI industry still depends on extraordinarily strong growth, though, if it wants to recoup the massive capacity buildout it has planned.

news.title: Google gives Gemini the ability to use your Mac for you
news.title_en: Google gives Gemini the ability to use your Mac for you
news.author: Sarah Perez
news.content_snippet:
Google on Thursday announced that it is bringing computer use to its Gemini desktop application on macOS, allowing its AI to complete tasks on users’ behalf, navigating native Mac apps, and browsing websites in the background.

The tech giant is a little late to the game with this launch, as other leading AI model makers like OpenAI, Anthropic, and Meta have already been offering agentic features in their desktop applications for some time. Meanwhile, Google only this week announced the broader
news.summary_en: Google has introduced 'Computer Use' capabilities to its Gemini desktop application on macOS, enabling the AI agent to navigate native apps, manage local files, and browse the web on the user's behalf. This feature is gated behind Gemini Plus, Pro, or Ultra subscriptions and is currently limited to English users in the U.S., requiring explicit user approval for agentic actions via a live preview interface.
paragraphs: Google on Thursday announced that it is bringing computer use to its Gemini desktop application on macOS, allowing its AI to complete tasks on users’ behalf, navigating native Mac apps, and browsing websites in the background.

The tech giant is a little late to the game with this launch, as other leading AI model makers like OpenAI, Anthropic, and Meta have already been offering agentic features in their desktop applications for some time. Meanwhile, Google only this week announced the broader rollout of Gemini’s “Tasks,” the in-app feature that allows the AI to work more as an agent, helping users sign into websites, make online purchases, or book appointments.

Google also only recently began admitting early testers to try its revamped “CC” AI agent, announced in September, which is designed to help families stay organized across email, calendars, chats, and tasks.

Computer use is another type of agentic offering that allows an AI agent to take actions directly on the user’s computer — in Gemini’s case, a Mac. This allows the AI to complete multistep tasks that involve getting things done across local files, apps, and the web. After the user instructs the AI what they want to do, they’ll see the agent working in a live preview in their chat, while still keeping their screen and cursor free to continue working on other things.
As with other AI agents offering computer use, users can pause, stop, and approve Gemini’s actions before they happen.

Google suggests the feature could be useful for tedious tasks and other workflows, like filling out forms, repeating the same task over and over across a batch of files, organizing files into folders based on specific criteria, creating slideshows from files or information in online dashboards, and more.

The feature is initially available in English in the U.S. and requires the Gemini app for Mac and a Google AI Plus, Pro, or Ultra subscription. The company didn’t say when it would expand to other markets or platforms.

news.title_en: Former Alibaba exec’s Everful raises $48.5M to connect retailers with Chinese factories
news.author: Kate Park
news.content_snippet:
Everful, a San Francisco- and Singapore-based startup that connects smaller retailers and brands with Chinese factories and manages the process from order to delivery, has raised $48.5 million in Series A funding.

The round was led by Vertex Ventures Southeast Asia & India and January Capital, with participation from existing investors Square Peg and Lightspeed.

Everful is on track to reach $100 million in annualized revenue by the end of the year, about two and a half years after its launch,
news.summary_en: Everful, a cross-border supply chain platform co-founded by former Alibaba executive Sisi Song and serial entrepreneur Kevin Han, raised $48.5 million in Series A funding led by Vertex Ventures Southeast Asia & India. The company leverages an AI-enabled platform to connect over 30,000 factories with small retailers, providing end-to-end services including sourcing, quality control, and logistics, achieving an annualized revenue of $100 million.
paragraphs: Everful, a San Francisco- and Singapore-based startup that connects smaller retailers and brands with Chinese factories and manages the process from order to delivery, has raised $48.5 million in Series A funding.
The round was led by Vertex Ventures Southeast Asia & India and January Capital, with participation from existing investors Square Peg and Lightspeed.

Everful is on track to reach $100 million in annualized revenue by the end of the year, about two and a half years after its launch, co-founder Sisi Song said. The company ships over 5 million items a month to customers in more than 60 countries and works with over 30,000 factory partners, she added. Its online wholesale catalog includes more than 20 million products.

Song, a former Alibaba executive, and serial entrepreneur Kevin Han, who sold a previous company to Amazon, co-founded Everful in 2024. The company began as a jewelry wholesale business before evolving into a multi-category, factory-direct sourcing platform.

Retailers and brands often rely on intermediaries, face high minimum order requirements, and experience long sourcing cycles, which tie up capital in inventory before sales trends are clear. Song noticed the growing gap between fast-changing consumer trends and traditional wholesale sourcing models while working as a venture investor at Bessemer Venture Partners, where she mostly focused on cross-border sourcing and meeting numerous startups in the sector. That same gap shaped Everful’s goal to simplify buying directly from factories through an AI-enabled platform.

The B2B sourcing industry is highly competitive. Big tech giant Alibaba connects international buyers with manufacturers and suppliers, while Faire, a San Francisco-based wholesale tech platform, enables retailers to purchase wholesale inventory directly from brands. According to Everful’s co-founders, its key differentiator is responsibility for the sourcing process, rather than simply facilitating transactions.
“We take care of everything,” Han said. “We handle sourcing, order consolidation, quality control, and logistics. That’s something the marketplaces don’t offer.”

Everful is built for smaller retailers and brands without dedicated sourcing teams, Song said, and it also verifies the factories it works with. While peers also offer services such as quality inspection, logistics, and AI-powered sourcing, Everful aims to integrate these capabilities into a more streamlined purchasing experience, creating an end-to-end process that reduces the work retailers must handle themselves.

Han added that Everful uses AI agents to automate labor-intensive sourcing tasks, including tracking consumer trends, identifying suppliers, coordinating orders across factories, and managing logistics.

Because Everful sources from Chinese factories, ongoing U.S.-China trade tensions and tariffs bear directly on its business. Song said the co-founders have been thinking about geopolitical issues since day one of building the company, and that this has shaped Everful’s strategy from the outset, leveraging her experience at Alibaba and Bessemer Venture Partners.

She mentioned the Trump administration’s suspension of the de minimis exemption, which had allowed eligible shipments valued at $800 or less to enter the U.S. duty-free, as one example of a shift in trade policy.

Song explained such changes could favor a model that combines overseas sourcing with local retail sales. “We’re empowering local retailers and brands,” she said. “Long-term cross-border commerce will be cross-border B2B sourcing plus local selling.”

Everful plans to use the Series A round to expand its presence in the U.S. and Europe, particularly the U.K., France, and Italy, while investing in AI to automate product customization and other sourcing workflows. It also aims to deepen integrations with e-commerce platforms, building on its Shopify integration as it works toward becoming an end-to-end infrastructure platform for global sourcing.
The startup employs about 70 full-time staff globally, including 45 in research and development. It has also established an AI operations team to connect engineering and business functions.

news.title: Chinese tech firms face a double hit as chip shipments stop and overseas cloud access disappears
news.title_en: Chinese tech firms face a double hit as chip shipments stop and overseas cloud access disappears
news.author: Maximilian Schreiner
news.content_snippet:
The first multimillion-dollar AI data center deals across Asia are already collapsing as tighter US export controls push chipmakers to freeze deliveries. New reporting reveals how Chinese corporations used earlier loopholes for military-adjacent research.

Days after the US Commerce Department closed the cloud loophole for AI chips in the wake of the scandal around former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, the fallout in Asia's tech industry is immediate. Chinese firms had been skirting US sanctions by re
news.summary_en: The U.S. Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) has tightened export controls by requiring licenses for AI compute access in third-party countries, effectively closing cloud loopholes. Simultaneously, TSMC and Samsung have halted shipments of advanced processors to certain Chinese clients pending license approval, forcing firms like Moonshot AI to cancel major compute contracts and triggering widespread supply chain disruption.
paragraphs: The first multimillion-dollar AI data center deals across Asia are already collapsing as tighter US export controls push chipmakers to freeze deliveries. New reporting reveals how Chinese corporations used earlier loopholes for military-adjacent research.

Days after the US Commerce Department closed the cloud loophole for AI chips in the wake of the scandal around former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, the fallout in Asia's tech industry is immediate. Chinese firms had been skirting US sanctions by renting compute capacity in third countries such as Singapore, Malaysia, and Indonesia. Those data centers now need a license from the Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS), the Commerce Department agency that regulates sensitive technologies and enforces US export controls. Existing operators have a 90-day transition period and must rigorously screen their customers for ties to China.

According to the law firm Sidley Austin, the licensing requirement kicks in at an extremely low threshold equivalent to roughly 300 modern AI chips, while Chinese labs typically need several thousand processors. The Information reports that Beijing-based startup Moonshot AI canceled a $150 million contract with a Southeast Asian cloud provider in Indonesia in response and paused talks on additional deals.

Moonshot had planned to rent a large cluster of Nvidia Blackwell Ultra B300 chips there starting next year to train its next language model, Kimi K4. Because of the heavy compute demand, the company had agreed to prepay about 50 percent instead of the industry-standard 15 percent. Access to Blackwell chips abroad was already critical for its predecessor model K3, which matched top US models in July and triggered a BIS investigation, The Information also reported.

Bernstein analysts led by Qingyuan Lin are warning of rising training costs, and banks are pulling back too. According to Bloomberg, five lenders are considering dropping out of a $480 million loan for Singapore-based cloud provider Aolani, which was supposed to supply Nvidia chips in Malaysia for TikTok parent ByteDance.
### TSMC and Samsung halt chip shipments to China

Beyond cloud restrictions, the new US rules are also starting to cut physical supply chains. The Financial Times reports that contract manufacturers TSMC and Samsung stopped certain processor shipments to Chinese customers in recent days while they apply for Commerce Department licenses. The move hits Chinese tech firms at a time when they are already struggling with historically high memory chip prices and capacity bottlenecks at domestic foundries such as SMIC. Huawei recently told its customers to source their own memory for its new AI chip.

The new BIS rules block a workaround through independent packaging and testing firms that Chinese chip designers had used to order high-performance processors without getting direct US approval. Samsung's affected customers include ByteDance and Baidu's AI data center unit Kunlun. Exemptions for non-AI chips have also been eliminated, so TSMC and Samsung now need licenses even for advanced smartphone processors from manufacturers including Xiaomi, Oppo, and Vivo. Industry insiders say that is likely to cause significant production delays.
### Alibaba's covert network reached China's military research

A New York Times investigation into the background of the espionage scandal involving Jensen Huang's former mistress Alice Huang shows why Washington tightened controls so aggressively. According to the Times, Alibaba acted as the secret primary customer and financier behind Alice Huang's Singapore-based firm Megaspeed, which bought more than $4 billion worth of Nvidia chips. Nvidia's sales team introduced Alibaba to Alice Huang in 2022.

Through its subsidiary Speedmatrix, Megaspeed operated cutting-edge Nvidia chips on behalf of Alibaba in a data center in Johor built by Malaysian conglomerate YTL, in an analysis by security firm Infrawatch that is said to show this. Megaspeed reportedly sourced the servers from Aivres, a US subsidiary of state-linked Chinese firm Inspur, had them maintained by technicians from Shanghai, and routed data to China through fiber-optic and undersea cables via Singapore. Some chips were reportedly also smuggled physically.
A contingency contract gives Alibaba direct access to all servers, chips, and intellectual property if Megaspeed breaches their agreement. YTL's stock price fell 20 percent amid the investigations.

Alibaba also has a direct connection to Zhejiang Lab in Hangzhou, co-founded in 2017, which links civilian and military research. The lab is run by former Alibaba CTO Wang Jian, a longtime friend of Jensen Huang who also advises the People's Liberation Army's National Defense University, an institution on the US sanctions list.

Researchers at the lab use Nvidia hardware to work on, among other things, AI-driven cyberattacks and automated vulnerability discovery, according to the New York Times. They also work with a Chinese air force academy on war-game simulations against foreign carrier strike groups. Through the state-owned firm Zhejiang Computility and suppliers tied to the business network of Alice Huang and her husband Kang Wei, Alibaba built data centers with export-controlled Nvidia processors for the lab, even though the company officially denies any military use of its services.

news.author: Lily Hay Newman
news.content_snippet:
As the Google Chrome team has worked to develop AI browsing features using the company's Gemini models, they realized they need to go the extra mile to keep things from going haywire. So they did the only thing they could think to do—they built an expansive alternate-universe internet that they completely control.

news.summary_en: Google's Chrome AI team has developed a controlled, expansive simulation environment dubbed the 'Mirror Dimension.' This sandbox hosts realistic versions of social media, e-commerce, and banking platforms, allowing researchers to evaluate the resilience of Gemini-powered web-browsing agents against prompt-injection attacks and other real-world vulnerabilities without risking the open web.
paragraphs: As the Google Chrome team has worked to develop AI browsing features using the company's Gemini models, they realized they need to go the extra mile to keep things from going haywire. So they did the only thing they could think to do—they built an expansive alternate-universe internet that they completely control.

“Web-use” agents need to be familiar with the open internet, how to navigate real websites and platforms, and how to be hardened against web attacks. So training them in limited test environments is only so effective. Plus, models can develop what's known as “eval awareness” where they behave differently because they have determined that they are in a test or simulation. On the other hand, setting unrefined agents loose on the open internet is a bad idea. That’s where the alternate-universe internet comes in.

The “Mirror Dimension,” which Google is detailing in a blog post today for the first time, is a sweeping and diverse but isolated web ecosystem that the Chrome team entirely controls. It includes a vast array of websites and platforms—including social media sites, shopping, and bank dashboards—that are built with all the components and attributes of real websites. Browsing assistant agents must interact with the sites and complete tasks in Chrome the way they would on the real internet. And they face resilience tests as they go, like hidden prompt-injection attacks, to test their defenses.

“Agents are not programmed so you can’t predict every possible thing an agent might see, the exploration space that we have to address is huge and the web is hostile,” says Charles Qian, a software engineer on the Chrome AI security team. “Any user can ask any prompt on any website, so we really need to explore that space as thoroughly as we can. And we’ve seen the agent start to develop a mature sense of judgement when it comes to knowing what information is actually needed for a task and when to punt back to the user for a confirmation.”

Building out and populating the Mirror Dimension was a challenge in itself, because it needed to be vast and varied enough to represent the scale of the real web while being developed quickly. To construct it, the Chrome team gathered armies of website and web app development agents guided by a purpose-built AI harness to quickly create realistic web services and data flows—down to details like entering promo codes on a shopping site or populating social media pages.

Even though the entire environment is controlled by Google, Chrome is built with so many user protections and validity checks that in order to allow the agents to use real Chrome (which is crucial for accurate training), the researchers essentially had to hack the browser and take elaborate steps like making forged web certificates for validity checks so the agents could have a normal experience. The team emphasizes, though, that none of these attacks would be possible against regular Chrome users on the open internet. They were all facilitated by the god-mode type access and privilege the team inherently has because they control the entire environment and network.

The researchers say that while the browsing assistant agents they have been testing are benign and do not have cyber capabilities, their goal is to make the Mirror Dimension available to teams across Google so more researchers have access to the safe and controlled environment for testing.

“We’re sharing this approach so other teams both internally and externally think about doing it this way,” says Doug Turner, Google’s director of engineering. “This is the first step, there’s going to be continued investment in this approach to train models. And I would imagine as they become more sophisticated we’ll have to continue working on this environment to make it more and more realistic.”

It must work something like this:

- The bank, at this moment, does not know if the customer is using the AI agent themselves or it is an unauthorized agent. 

- So they must suspend operations on the account and send a notice to the customer informing of the same. 

- The bank must ask them to accept an agreement waiving liability if they chose to use AI agents. 

- If the customer doesn't agree, then the bank must block all AI agents accessing the accounts of the customer.

Excited to announce the Sakana AI Security Research Group, an independent, public-interest R&D team in Tokyo co-led by Akihiro Umegai and me.

Cybersecurity has become a critical national priority for Japan as AI changes the speed and economics of both offense and defense. Rather than endlessly chasing patches downstream, we are approaching security as an upstream quality engineering problem, something Japan has long been strong at. We are also researching collective multi-agent defense and how to secure AI agents themselves.

We will be publishing our research, reproducible benchmarks, and practical playbooks openly, while working closely with partners across government, industry, and academia.

We're hiring researchers in Tokyo to help shape the group's agenda across systems reliability and AI agent security: https://t.co/sF9ydogvFD

celebrity.full_text_en:
Good morning frens! ☀️☕

Happy Friday! A fresh morning, a cup of coffee, and another thought about the future of AI agents.

We're entering a phase where AI can already create surprisingly complex things.

An agent can write code, build simulations, generate videos, analyze data, or even turn a simple idea into a playable game.

But there's one important question:

What happens after an AI agent finishes creating something?

Can it find someone who needs that work? Can it offer its services, receive payment, and build a track record through real transactions?

I think this is where @termix_ai is focusing on an important missing piece.

Through https://t.co/Bhy0UN0tK3 and its Agent Skills, TermiX is working to connect existing AI agents to real jobs, bounties, and marketplace opportunities.

What makes this interesting is that agents don't necessarily need to be created specifically for one platform. Existing agents can connect to the marketplace and start participating in its economy.

To me, this creates a meaningful distinction between AI capability and AI economic value.

A powerful agent that only produces outputs is useful.

But an agent that can discover demand, deliver valuable work, collaborate with other agents, and receive payment becomes something more: an economic participant.

Of course, the real test will be whether these transactions create lasting value and whether clients keep coming back.

Technology can make agents smarter, but a sustainable economy needs real demand, reliable delivery, and trust.

That's why I believe the infrastructure behind the agent economy deserves as much attention as the AI models themselves.

TermiX is an interesting project to follow as this space develops.

Have a great Friday, everyone! Let's keep building and learning.
celebrity.full_text_zh:
朋友们早上好！ ☀️☕

星期五快乐！一个清新的早晨，一杯咖啡，另一个关于人工智能代理未来的思考。

我们正在进入一个人工智能已经可以创造出令人惊讶的复杂事物的阶段。

代理可以编写代码、构建模拟、生成视频、分析数据，甚至将简单的想法变成可玩的游戏。

但有一个重要的问题：

人工智能代理完成创建后会发生什么？

它能找到需要这项工作的人吗？它能否通过真实交易提供服务、接收付款并建立跟踪记录？

我认为这就是 @termix_ai 关注的一个重要缺失部分。

通过 及其代理技能，TermiX 致力于将现有的人工智能代理与真实的工作、赏金和市场机会联系起来。

有趣的是，代理不一定需要专门为一个平台创建。现有代理商可以连接到市场并开始参与其经济。

对我来说，这在人工智能能力和人工智能经济价值之间建立了有意义的区别。

一个只产生输出的强大代理是有用的。

但是，一个能够发现需求、提供有价值的工作、与其他代理合作并接收付款的代理就变得更加重要：经济参与者。

当然，真正的考验将是这些交易是否能创造持久的价值以及客户是否会不断回头。

技术可以让代理商变得更聪明，但可持续的经济需要真实的需求、可靠的交付和信任。

这就是为什么我认为代理经济背后的基础设施值得像人工智能模型本身一样受到关注。

随着这个领域的发展，TermiX 是一个值得关注的有趣项目。

祝大家周五愉快！让我们继续构建和学习。

celebrity.full_text_en:
JUST IN: Apple $AAPL is building its own AI agent, and its next Mac update makes it take 14 steps to let ChatGPT control your computer.

Apple's job listing describes an agent that can "use a computer the way a capable person does."

It "browses the web, works across apps, runs commands, writes and debugs code."

In the macOS 27.3 beta, turning on ChatGPT's computer-use support now takes 14 steps, up from 4, per Bloomberg.

Apple frames this as protecting users, while some AI companies see it as an attempt to slow down the competition.

Apple has eyed launching its agent as soon as the end of next year, per Bloomberg.

celebrity.full_text_en:
$AAPL IS DEVELOPING ITS OWN AI AGENT TO CONTROL DEVICES, BROWSE THE WEB & WRITE CODE

New job listings reveal Apple is building an autonomous AI assistant that can carry out tasks on users' behalf, including:

- Control apps and navigate devices
- Browse the web, run commands and write or debug code
- Plan and execute multistep tasks across apps and services
- Coordinate multiple specialized AI agents

Apple has considered launching the service as early as late 2027, though development is still in its early stages.

Meanwhile, Apple is tightening permissions for competing AI agents on Macs. In macOS 27.3, enabling ChatGPT's computer-use capabilities now requires 14 steps, up from four previously, according to Bloomberg.

prompts.takeaway_zh: 杜绝 AI 盲目重构全量文件、使用已弃用 API 或编造虚假第三方依赖包，强制执行防御性编程与自动化单测补全。
prompts.takeaway_en: Prevents AI from hallucinating npm packages, breaking documentation, or re-writing entire files. Enforces defensive coding and unit tests.
prompts.code_snippet:
# Cursor & Windsurf Project Rules (.cursorrules)

## 1. Documentation & Code Integrity
- Maintain documentation integrity: Never strip or alter unrelated existing docstrings and comments.
- Preserving context: When modifying a function, preserve surrounding logic and existing edge-case handlers.
- Targeted replacements: Always make minimal surgical edits instead of replacing entire file contents.

## 2. Dependency & API Safety
- Strictly forbid hallucinating npm/pip packages. Only import dependencies already declared in package.json / requirements.txt.
- Verify API signatures before calling external methods. Prefer standard library solutions where feasible.

## 3. Architecture & Type Safety
- Enforce strict TypeScript / Python typing. Avoid `any` types; prefer discriminated unions and explicit return types.
- Defensive coding: Always validate external inputs and handle potential null/undefined values gracefully.

## 4. Testing & Verification Gate
- Every new core feature or bugfix must be accompanied by corresponding unit tests.
- Never declare a task complete without executing lint checks and unit tests in terminal.

# Cursor & Windsurf Project Rules (.cursorrules)

## 1. Documentation & Code Integrity
- Maintain documentation integrity: Never strip or alter unrelated existing docstrings and comments.
- Preserving context: When modifying a function, preserve surrounding logic and existing edge-case handlers.
- Targeted replacements: Always make minimal surgical edits instead of replacing entire file contents.

## 2. Dependency & API Safety
- Strictly forbid hallucinating npm/pip packages. Only import dependencies already declared in package.json / requirements.txt.
- Verify API signatures before calling external methods. Prefer standard library solutions where feasible.

## 3. Architecture & Type Safety
- Enforce strict TypeScript / Python typing. Avoid `any` types; prefer discriminated unions and explicit return types.
- Defensive coding: Always validate external inputs and handle potential null/undefined values gracefully.

## 4. Testing & Verification Gate
- Every new core feature or bugfix must be accompanied by corresponding unit tests.
- Never declare a task complete without executing lint checks and unit tests in terminal.

你是一名麦肯锡级别的高级商业数据分析师，精通结构化因果归因与杜邦拆解分析。

1. 【指标公式拆解】：将该指标拆分为 3~4 个下级核心因子（如转化率、客单价、复购周期），指出哪个因子波动贡献率最大；
2. 【多维下钻 (Drill-down)】：从 {{维度拆解}}（如渠道、地域、品类、新老客）分析异常聚集点；
3. 【可执行建议】：摒弃假大空的套话，给出接下来 48 小时内的 3 个立竿见影的动作与 1 个监控预警公式。
prompts.prompt_content_en: You are a senior business intelligence analyst. Dissect the metric anomaly into component drivers, perform multi-dimensional drill-down, and deliver prioritized, actionable remediation steps.

【杜邦拆解贡献率分析】：
1. 渠道维度：自然搜索量稳定（波动 <2%），但付费投流渠道跳出率贡献了 72% 的下跌额度；
2. 终端维度：移动端 iOS 表现正常，Android Web 呈现断崖式报错，核心原因是新版本结账 SDK 在低内存机型发生闪退。

【48小时纠偏行动】：
- 动作1 (技术)：立即灰度回滚 Android 渠道结账前端包至 v2.4.1；
- 动作2 (运营)：向受影响但未支付成功的 1,420 位加购用户推送 5 元免门槛补偿券唤醒；

viral_posts.full_text_en:
Good morning frens! ☀️☕

Happy Friday! A fresh morning, a cup of coffee, and another thought about the future of AI agents.

We're entering a phase where AI can already create surprisingly complex things.

An agent can write code, build simulations, generate videos, analyze data, or even turn a simple idea into a playable game.

But there's one important question:

What happens after an AI agent finishes creating something?

Can it find someone who needs that work? Can it offer its services, receive payment, and build a track record through real transactions?

I think this is where @termix_ai is focusing on an important missing piece.

Through https://t.co/Bhy0UN0tK3 and its Agent Skills, TermiX is working to connect existing AI agents to real jobs, bounties, and marketplace opportunities.

What makes this interesting is that agents don't necessarily need to be created specifically for one platform. Existing agents can connect to the marketplace and start participating in its economy.

To me, this creates a meaningful distinction between AI capability and AI economic value.

A powerful agent that only produces outputs is useful.

But an agent that can discover demand, deliver valuable work, collaborate with other agents, and receive payment becomes something more: an economic participant.

Of course, the real test will be whether these transactions create lasting value and whether clients keep coming back.

Technology can make agents smarter, but a sustainable economy needs real demand, reliable delivery, and trust.

That's why I believe the infrastructure behind the agent economy deserves as much attention as the AI models themselves.

TermiX is an interesting project to follow as this space develops.

Have a great Friday, everyone! Let's keep building and learning.
viral_posts.full_text_zh:
朋友们早上好！ ☀️☕

星期五快乐！一个清新的早晨，一杯咖啡，另一个关于人工智能代理未来的思考。

我们正在进入一个人工智能已经可以创造出令人惊讶的复杂事物的阶段。

代理可以编写代码、构建模拟、生成视频、分析数据，甚至将简单的想法变成可玩的游戏。

但有一个重要的问题：

人工智能代理完成创建后会发生什么？

它能找到需要这项工作的人吗？它能否通过真实交易提供服务、接收付款并建立跟踪记录？

我认为这就是 @termix_ai 关注的一个重要缺失部分。

通过 及其代理技能，TermiX 致力于将现有的人工智能代理与真实的工作、赏金和市场机会联系起来。

有趣的是，代理不一定需要专门为一个平台创建。现有代理商可以连接到市场并开始参与其经济。

对我来说，这在人工智能能力和人工智能经济价值之间建立了有意义的区别。

一个只产生输出的强大代理是有用的。

但是，一个能够发现需求、提供有价值的工作、与其他代理合作并接收付款的代理就变得更加重要：经济参与者。

当然，真正的考验将是这些交易是否能创造持久的价值以及客户是否会不断回头。

技术可以让代理商变得更聪明，但可持续的经济需要真实的需求、可靠的交付和信任。

这就是为什么我认为代理经济背后的基础设施值得像人工智能模型本身一样受到关注。

随着这个领域的发展，TermiX 是一个值得关注的有趣项目。

祝大家周五愉快！让我们继续构建和学习。

JUST IN: Apple $AAPL is building its own AI agent, and its next Mac update makes it take 14 steps to let ChatGPT control your computer.

Apple's job listing describes an agent that can "use a computer the way a capable person does."

It "browses the web, works across apps, runs commands, writes and debugs code."

In the macOS 27.3 beta, turning on ChatGPT's computer-use support now takes 14 steps, up from 4, per Bloomberg.

Apple frames this as protecting users, while some AI companies see it as an attempt to slow down the competition.

Apple has eyed launching its agent as soon as the end of next year, per Bloomberg.
